recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Do not widen Reference.identifier for this issue; any future multiple-identifier core change would require a new normative-change decision.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core issue requesting Reference.identifier cardinality 0..* so logical references could carry multiple business identifiers; Jira resolved it as a duplicate of FHIR-30878.
initial_application: No FHIR-36212-specific source-changing commit was found. The duplicate target FHIR-30878 was applied by git commit 0bdbd05b41b1a83334cde1e26cfb7d30a59b6e72, which updated source/datatypes/reference.xml to keep Reference.identifier single-valued and add additionalIdentifier extension guidance.
additional_context: FHIR-30878 resolved that normative rules prevent widening Reference.identifier max cardinality and selected a standard extension instead. Zulip and FHIR-I minutes confirm the multiple-logical-identifier use case, the normative-break concern, the FHIR-30878 Persuasive with Modification vote, and the FHIR-36212 duplicate vote. The extension is now defined in the FHIR Extension Pack for Reference with max * Identifier values, and the current CI build links to it.
reconciliation: No source change was made because current build-scope source already has Reference.identifier max 0..1 and directs additional identifiers to http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/additionalIdentifier, matching the final duplicate-target decision.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-36212 explicitly duplicates FHIR-30878, whose accepted resolution selected the additionalIdentifier extension instead of changing Reference.identifier max cardinality.
A later/current reconciliation edited adjacent Reference.identifier scope wording but preserved the FHIR-30878 single-identifier plus extension outcome.
